question: Pipe P can fill (3)/(4) part of a tank in 27 hours, and pipe Q can fill (2)/(3) part of the same tank in 12 hours. Both P and Q were kept open for 6 hours, then both were closed. Pipe R alone was then opened and it emptied the water in the tank in 8 hours. Pipes P, Q and R together can fill the empty tank in:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Time to fill full tank: P = 27 × 4/3 = 36 hours, Q = 12 × 3/2 = 18 hours.

In 6 hours, part filled by P and Q = 6 × (1/36 + 1/18) = 1/2 tank.

Pipe R empties this 1/2 tank in 8 hours ⇒ Full tank empty time for R = 16 hours.

Let total capacity = LCM(36, 18, 16) = 144 units.

Net efficiency of (P + Q − R) = (144 ÷ 36) + (144 ÷ 18) − (144 ÷ 16) = 4 + 8 − 9 = 3 units/hour.

**∴ The correct answer is 48 hours.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time taken by P to fill 3/4 part of the tank = 27 hours.

⇒ Total time taken by P to fill the empty tank = 27 × 4/3 = 36 hours.

Time taken by Q to fill 2/3 part of the tank = 12 hours.

⇒ Total time taken by Q to fill the empty tank = 12 × 3/2 = 18 hours.

Part filled by P and Q in 6 hours = 6 × (1/36 + 1/18) = 6 × (3/36) = 1/2.

Pipe R empties this 1/2 tank in 8 hours.

⇒ Total time taken by R alone to empty the full tank = 8 × 2 = 16 hours.

**Calculations:**

⇒ Net efficiency of P, Q, and R together = 4 + 8 − 9 = 3 units/hour.

⇒ Time taken by P, Q, and R to fill the tank = Total Work ÷ Net Efficiency

⇒ Time taken = 144 ÷ 3 = 48 hours.

**∴ The correct answer is 48 hours.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Inlet and Outlet Pipes

If a pipe fills a tank in x hours, its efficiency is taken as positive (1/x). If an outlet pipe empties the tank in y hours, its efficiency is taken as negative (−1/y).

LCM Method for Time & Work

Total work is assumed as the LCM of all the given individual times. Efficiency is calculated as Total Work ÷ Time taken. The total time for combined work = Total Work ÷ Net Efficiency.

Part of Tank Filled or Emptied

The fraction of the tank filled or emptied in a given time period is equal to the Time taken × Rate of work (Combined Efficiency).
